requirement:
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> {"search_id":"11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111","used":["1"]}. Entries
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
rationale:
The requirement's only structural obligation is that the `finish_search` tool's MCP description is the quoted text. The sole implementation root is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#impl[Session<'_, D>/ToolSession<D>]/fn[definitions]`. It defines a `finish_search` tool whose `description` string matches the required text word for word. That covers every sentence of the requirement:

- The opening sentence about closing a delivered search and recording dependencies.
- The `search_id` and `used` explanation, including the example JSON, which the Rust string escapes correctly.
- The sentences on omitting entries and on `used:[]`.
- The sentence that every delivered search must be finished.
- The sentence on the `{search_id, finished:true}` result.

The same definition also declares a parameter schema with `search_id` as a uuid-format string and `used` as an array of strings. Both are required and `additionalProperties` is false. This matches the description and conflicts with nothing in it. The `references` lookup shows no other implementation sites, and no refining declarations were supplied. The requirement states no behavior beyond the description text, so there is no behavioral obligation to assess. No {fixme} acknowledgments are present, and I found no gaps.
